editorialNote: Focused KB for type 1 diabetes. The therapeutic landscape split: (1) insulin therapy + automated insulin delivery (closed-loop pumps: Medtronic 780G, Tandem Control-IQ, Omnipod 5, iLet Bionic Pancreas); (2) continuous glucose monitors (Dexcom G6/G7, Libre 2/3, Medtronic Guardian 4); (3) FIRST-EVER disease-modifying therapy — teplizumab (Tzield, FDA 2022) for delaying T1D onset in at-risk individuals; (4) allogeneic islet cell therapy — donislecel (Lantidra, FDA 2023) for labile-T1D adults. Any T1D output that fails to mention teplizumab is out of date.

lifestyleCategories: Structured T1D education (DSMES/DAFNE-style carbohydrate counting + insulin dose adjustment)
Continuous glucose monitor (CGM) for all T1D — current ADA standard
Consider automated insulin delivery (AID / hybrid closed-loop) for most T1D patients
Exercise planning — pre/intra/post-exercise carb and insulin adjustments to prevent hypoglycemia
Celiac disease screening at diagnosis + periodically (TTG IgA)
Thyroid screening at diagnosis + yearly (TSH + anti-TPO)
Annual retinal exam starting ~5 years post-diagnosis (or from puberty)
Annual UACR (urine albumin-creatinine ratio) for nephropathy screening
Glucagon prescription (nasal Baqsimi, auto-injector Gvoke) for all patients and caregivers

items.title: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care in Diabetes — 2025
items.authors: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
items.summary: Annual ADA Standards of Care — the single most cited US diabetes guideline. Chapter 7 (diabetes technology) endorses CGM and AID for all T1D; chapter 9 covers pharmacologic approaches. Updated annually.

items.title: The Effect of Intensive Treatment of Diabetes on the Development and Progression of Long-term Complications in Insulin-Dependent Diabetes Mellitus (DCCT)
items.summary: Foundational RCT of intensive vs conventional insulin therapy in 1,441 T1D patients over mean 6.5 years. Intensive therapy reduced retinopathy progression by ~60%, nephropathy by ~50%, neuropathy by ~60%. EDIC follow-up showed 'metabolic memory' — early intensive control continues benefit for decades.

keyPassages.quote: Intensive therapy reduced the adjusted mean risk for the development of retinopathy by 76 percent.

items.title: An Anti-CD3 Antibody, Teplizumab, in Relatives at Risk for Type 1 Diabetes (TN-10)
items.authors: Herold KC, Bundy BN, Long SA, et al. (Type 1 Diabetes TrialNet Study Group)
items.summary: Phase 2 prevention trial of 14-day IV teplizumab (anti-CD3) vs placebo in 76 relatives of T1D patients with ≥2 autoantibodies + dysglycemia (stage 2 T1D). Median time to diabetes was 48.4 months with teplizumab vs 24.4 months with placebo (HR 0.41, P=0.006) — a median 2-year delay in onset. Basis for Tzield FDA approval.

keyPassages.quote: The median time from randomization to the diagnosis of clinical type 1 diabetes was 48.4 months in the teplizumab group versus 24.4 months in the placebo group.

items.title: TZIELD (teplizumab-mzwv) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: FIRST-EVER disease-modifying therapy for type 1 diabetes. FDA-approved November 2022 to delay stage 3 T1D in adults and pediatric patients ≥8 years with stage 2 T1D (≥2 islet autoantibodies + dysglycemia). 14-day IV infusion course. Warnings: cytokine release syndrome (first days), lymphopenia, serious infections, hypersensitivity.

keyPassages.quote: TZIELD is indicated to delay the onset of Stage 3 type 1 diabetes (T1D) in adults and pediatric patients aged 8 years and older who currently have Stage 2 T1D.

items.title: LANTIDRA (donislecel-jujn) — US FDA Prescribing Information
items.summary: First FDA-approved allogeneic pancreatic islet cellular therapy for adults with T1D who experience severe hypoglycemia and impaired awareness of hypoglycemia despite intensive management. Approved June 2023. Requires chronic immunosuppression. Complicated logistics limit real-world use.

keyPassages.quote: LANTIDRA is an allogeneic pancreatic islet cellular therapy indicated for the treatment of adults with type 1 diabetes who are unable to approach target HbA1c because of current repeated episodes of severe hypoglycemia despite intensive diabetes management.

canonicalFacts.claim: Teplizumab (Tzield, Provention/Sanofi) is the first FDA-approved disease-modifying therapy for T1D (November 2022) — delays stage 3 T1D by median ~2 years in stage 2 individuals.
Donislecel (Lantidra, CellTrans) — first FDA-approved allogeneic pancreatic islet cellular therapy (June 2023) for hypoglycemia-unaware adults with T1D.

redFlags: Evidence does not support relying on 'honeymoon' remission or low insulin requirement to defer standard T1D management — beta-cell loss continues regardless.
Literature does not support recommending low-carb 'cure T1D' diets as replacement for insulin — T1D is not a diet-controlled disease.
Physicians generally caution against prescribing SGLT2 inhibitors for T1D without specialist co-management — increased risk of euglycemic DKA.
Literature warns against metformin monotherapy for T1D — it does not substitute for insulin; may be used as adjunct for insulin resistance in some adults.

Physicians generally caution against initiate teplizumab without confirming stage 2 T1D (≥2 islet autoantibodies + dysglycemia); it is not indicated in new-onset stage 3 T1D as of Nov 2022 approval (though PROTECT data supports that indication; regulatory status evolving).

pipelineDrugs.name: Teplizumab
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Humanized anti-CD3 monoclonal antibody — induces regulatory T cells
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved November 2022 to delay stage 3 T1D in stage 2 patients ≥8 years
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First disease-modifying T1D therapy. Omitting this is major AI slop.

pipelineDrugs.name: Donislecel
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved June 2023 for adults with T1D and problematic hypoglycemia
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: First FDA-approved islet cell therapy. Limited to hypoglycemia-unaware patients due to need for chronic immunosuppression.

pipelineDrugs.name: Insulin (analog portfolio)
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Backbone therapy. Modern ultra-rapid (Fiasp, Lyumjev) and ultra-long-acting (degludec) analogs replace older NPH/regular insulin.

pipelineDrugs.name: Automated Insulin Delivery systems
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Hybrid closed-loop / fully closed-loop pump + CGM algorithms
pipelineDrugs.sponsor: Tandem / Medtronic / Insulet / Beta Bionics / CamDiab
pipelineDrugs.status: FDA-approved; iLet 2023 is first 'no carb counting' fully adaptive system
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Current ADA-endorsed standard of care for T1D. Reduces severe hypoglycemia and improves time-in-range.

pipelineDrugs.name: Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGM)
pipelineDrugs.status: Multiple FDA-approved; OTC Stelo (Dexcom) approved 2024 for T2D non-insulin

pipelineDrugs.name: Verapamil (repurposing)
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: Calcium channel blocker — preserves beta cell mass by downregulating TXNIP
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Repurposing candidate with pilot data showing C-peptide preservation in new-onset T1D.

pipelineDrugs.name: Low-dose anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG)
pipelineDrugs.status: Phase 2 (Haller 2018/2021) showed C-peptide preservation and HbA1c improvement
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Repurposing of a transplant drug for T1D beta-cell preservation.

pipelineDrugs.name: Semaglutide (repurposing for T1D)
pipelineDrugs.mechanism: GLP-1 receptor agonist (adjunct in overweight/obese T1D)
pipelineDrugs.status: Investigational for T1D adjunctive use (case series and small trials); NOT FDA-approved for T1D
pipelineDrugs.whyItMatters: Off-label interest for T1D patients with obesity. Not a substitute for insulin.
